html:
SMTO-CTX-0008 — This task's saved model settings don't match the model

GUID: 7917249e-52d6-4f0b-b899-2e0ea0405ef2
Slug: configured-context-profile-mismatch
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: context

What happened

  • This task was saved expecting a model with a different amount of room than the one in use now. This older error doesn't say which setting differs.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main model, then Limits and recovery, and make sure Context ceiling is Auto or the server's real limit. A limit that doesn't match the model server is the usual cause of this mismatch.
  2. Open the old task and look through its steps to see what it already finished. This older error doesn't record how far the task got, so checking first stops you from repeating changes it already made.
  3. Start a new task that asks only for the work that is still left. Model settings apply to new tasks, so a new task uses the corrected limit.

What success looks like

  • The new task runs past its first steps without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't raise Output allowance to fix this, and don't delete the old task; its history shows what was already done.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A saved or configured context profile does not match the serving model's capacity; this retained compatibility error comes from an earlier SMTO version and no current code path raises it.

What this means

  • The retained compatibility identity describes a mismatch between configured/saved context assumptions and serving capacity; current preparation uses more specific profile and reservation checks. This identity remains for historical or external payloads; no live direct producer was found. Historical facts, including whether inference began, must come from the saved occurrence.

Why this can happen

  • The retained compatibility identity describes a mismatch between configured/saved context assumptions and serving capacity; current preparation uses more specific profile and reservation checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare any retained model identity, window and reservation before selecting a new task profile; do not infer exact capacity from this legacy category alone.

How to fix it

  • No current code path raises this retained compatibility error. Read the saved occurrence's runtime facts (model_request_started, context_window_tokens, reserved_output_tokens) to learn whether inference started and what capacity was assumed, set the routed role's Context ceiling (context_window_tokens) to Auto or the served model's real maximum length in Settings › Setup › Model routing, and continue the remaining work in a new task, because model configuration applies to new tasks.
  • Restore the saved model capacity before Resume, or start a new task with an accurate model profile.

Relevant SMTO settings

  • Open Context Window: model-configuration / llm_context_window_tokens. Applies to: new task.
  • Start a new task after changing this setting. Active and resumed tasks retain their captured values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended task profile and actual serving capacity pass current preparation and request preflight.

What not to do

  • Do not increase max completion tokens as the primary fix; reserving more output reduces input headroom.
  • Do not claim an inference response occurred when the model request did not start.

Technical notes

  • This identity remains for historical or external payloads; no live direct producer was found. Historical facts, including whether inference began, must come from the saved occurrence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-CTX-0002 — A step's results were too large to send to the model
  • SMTO-CTX-0003 — Your current request is too big for the model
  • SMTO-CTX-0004 — This step needs more room than the model has
  • SMTO-CTX-0005 — Your request and the model's answer won't fit together
  • SMTO-CTX-0006 — Your request is too large for SMTO to plan the task
  • SMTO-CTX-0007 — Provider tokenizer rejected context
